sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Montcalm County?
sections.html:
Deeds for Montcalm County land are recorded at the register of deeds in Stanton, the county seat. The office sits at 211 W. Main St., with a mailing address of P.O. Box 368, Stanton, MI 48888, and answers at 989-831-7337 according to the state Department of Treasury's county list. The county website also gives an email address for the office at regofdeeds@co.montcalm.mi.us.

Ask the office for its current counter hours and whether it takes electronic submissions before you plan a trip. Many sellers never visit in person, because the title company or closing attorney handling the sale carries the signed deed over and files it for them.

The register records and indexes. It does not draft deeds or give legal advice, so a seller who wants to add a spouse, remove a name or sign over a parcel should use an attorney or title company to prepare the paper first.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Montcalm County?
sections.html:
Montcalm County is a rural county in West Michigan that belongs to the Grand Rapids metropolitan area. It covers 721 square miles, of which 705 are land, and Greenville is its largest city. About 84.6% of residents live in rural areas, so a good share of sales involve acreage, a septic system, a private well or a house on a township road.

The Census Bureau counted 66,614 people in 2020 and estimated 69,406 for July 2025, a gain of 4.2%. Owners occupy 83.1% of homes, and the median value of an owner-occupied home was $185,500 for 2020 to 2024. Workers spend a mean 30.7 minutes getting to their jobs, which tells you many owners commute toward Greenville, Grand Rapids or beyond.

Eight public school districts serve the county, including Greenville Public Schools, Central Montcalm Public Schools, Lakeview Public Schools, Montabella Community Schools, Carson City Crystal Area School District, Tri County Area Schools and Vestaburg Community Schools, plus the Montcalm Area ISD. Buyers with children often ask which district a house falls in, so have the parcel's district ready.

  • Households here earned a median $67,344 in 2020 to 2024 dollars.
  • The county issued 201 building permits in 2025.
  • Median gross rent was $869, which gives some owners a rental fallback when they cannot sell quickly.

sections.h2: How much does recording a deed cost in Montcalm County?
sections.html:
State law sets the standard recording charge at $30.00 per document, whatever its page count, under MCL 600.2567. A document that assigns or discharges more than one instrument adds $3.00 for each extra instrument. Copies run $1.00 per page and certifying a recorded document costs $5.00.

The fee is due when the document is left for recording. The exceptions in the statute cover electronic filings paid within one business day, certain government filers and tax-foreclosure paperwork. Charter counties may set their own schedules, so confirm the amount with the Montcalm office if you are mailing a check.

  • Standard deed or mortgage: $30.00.
  • Each additional instrument assigned or discharged in one document: $3.00.
  • Copy of a record: $1.00 per page.
  • Certification of a recorded document: $5.00.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax does the seller pay in Montcalm County?
sections.html:
The seller owes it. State law puts the liability on the grantor, and the tax is paid to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered. Michigan counts two taxes: a state tax of $3.75 and a county tax of $0.55, each for every $500 of value or fraction of $500. The county rate applies to counties with fewer than 2,000,000 residents, which includes Montcalm.

The table works the rates through the county's median home value. Your actual bill depends on the price on the deed and on any exemption that applies.

Some transfers escape the state tax, for example a conveyance from a parent to a child or grandchild, and a deed given in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure. The county act lists no parent-to-child exemption, so the county portion can still apply. The exemption must be claimed on the face of the deed.

sections.h2: What does the register of deeds require on a deed?
sections.html:
MCL 565.201 lists what a deed must show before the register may accept it. A document that misses an item gets returned, which can push a closing date. Check each point with your title company before signing.

  • Each signer's name printed or typed beneath a black or dark blue signature, matching the name in the notary acknowledgment.
  • The address of every grantee, with a street number where street numbers are in common use.
  • The drafter's name and business address.
  • A top margin of at least 2.5 inches on page one and 0.5 inch on every other side.
  • A first line naming the single recordable event, such as warranty deed.
  • 10-point or larger type, black ink, white paper of at least 20-pound weight, sheets from 8.5 by 11 to 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Only the last four digits of any Social Security number.

The statute also requires an English translation attached to any instrument written partly or wholly in another language.

sections.h2: What happens to property taxes after a Montcalm County sale?
sections.html:
A sale resets the tax base. Michigan caps yearly growth in taxable value at the lesser of 5% or inflation, but a transfer of ownership lifts taxable value to the state equalized value for the following year, which is about half of market value. The buyer should expect a larger bill than the seller paid if the seller held the home for years.

The buyer must tell the local assessor about the transfer within 45 days on the state's property transfer affidavit. The register of deeds also reports recorded transactions to local assessors each month. Transfers to a spouse, to certain close relatives of residential property that is not used commercially, and through foreclosure carry exceptions, which is why a family transfer can keep the old taxable value.

If you claimed the principal residence exemption, file Form 2602 with your township or city assessor within 90 days after the house stops being your home. A late filing triggers a penalty of $5 a day, up to $200, and the exemption comes off the roll on December 31 of the year you file.

sections.h2: What if the house is inherited or needs repairs?
sections.html:
Inherited houses sell in Montcalm County the same way as any other, once the right person can sign. An estate usually needs the personal representative's authority, and a deed from the estate is recorded like any other. Bring a certified death certificate if a deed names a surviving owner.

A house with deferred repairs, a failed septic system or a title tangle can still close, though conventional buyers may walk away. A buyer who pays cash and takes the house as it stands removes the inspection and loan steps, and the same recording, transfer tax and affidavit rules apply on closing day. Ask the Montcalm treasurer for the tax status of the parcel before you set a closing date.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax when a house sells in Montcalm County?
faqs.a: The seller pays. Michigan law makes the grantor liable, and the money goes to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivering the deed. At a $185,500 price the combined state and county tax comes to $1,595.30.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee for a deed in Montcalm County?
faqs.a: The state fee is $30.00 per document under MCL 600.2567, with $3.00 more for each additional instrument assigned or discharged. Confirm with the Stanton office before mailing a check, since a county's own schedule can differ.

faqs.q: Does the register of deeds prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. Register offices record documents and do not draft them or give legal advice. A title company, attorney or your closing agent should prepare the deed so it meets the format rules in MCL 565.201.

faqs.q: Will my property taxes go up for the buyer after the sale?
faqs.a: Usually yes. A transfer of ownership resets taxable value to the state equalized value for the next year, and the buyer must report the transfer to the assessor within 45 days. Exceptions cover transfers to a spouse and certain family transfers of residential property.

faqs.q: How do I end my principal residence exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: File a Request to Rescind Principal Residence Exemption, Form 2602, with your local assessor within 90 days after the house stops being your home. Late filers face $5 a day up to $200, and the exemption leaves the roll on December 31.
